name: kube-apiserver
keywords: cluster API and policy boundary
canonical object interface
definition: The control-plane server that exposes the Kubernetes API and coordinates policy, conversion, persistence, reads, and watches.

name: etcd
keywords: strongly consistent API state store
Raft-backed persistence
definition: The distributed key-value store used by the API server to persist Kubernetes API state.

name: kube-controller-manager
keywords: built-in control loops
definition: The component that hosts many built-in controllers implementing Kubernetes API behavior.

name: kube-scheduler
keywords: choose a node for an unscheduled Pod
definition: The component that selects a feasible preferred node and records a Pod binding without starting containers.

name: kubelet
keywords: realize assigned Pods on a node
definition: The node agent that coordinates runtime, network, storage, probes, and status for assigned Pods.

name: authentication
keywords: establish caller identity and groups
definition: The API request stage that establishes the caller identity and group information used by later policy decisions.

name: authorization
keywords: allow a verb on a resource
RBAC decision
definition: The API request stage that decides whether an authenticated identity may perform the requested action.

name: admission control
keywords: mutate or validate API objects after authorization
definition: API-server processing that may default, mutate, validate, or reject resource requests after authorization.

name: admission webhook
keywords: synchronous external admission dependency
AdmissionReview
definition: A network service called by the API server with AdmissionReview objects to mutate or validate matching requests.

name: optimistic concurrency
keywords: reject stale writes
refetch and recompute
definition: The update discipline that detects stale resource versions and requires clients to recompute against current state.

name: reconciliation loop
keywords: observed state toward desired state
definition: A repeatable loop that observes current state, compares it with intent, and applies a bounded corrective action.

name: level-based reconciliation
keywords: current state is authority
events schedule work
definition: Reconciliation based on current desired and observed levels rather than replaying every historical event.

name: list-watch
keywords: snapshot plus change stream
resourceVersion
definition: The API pattern that obtains current collection state and streams later changes from its resource version.

name: shared informer
keywords: shared local cache and event handlers
definition: A client mechanism that maintains a local object cache from list-watch and distributes change notifications to handlers.

name: rate-limited workqueue
keywords: deduplicate keys and back off retries
definition: A queue of stable object keys that decouples watch notifications from retryable reconciliation workers.

name: Deployment
keywords: replaceable Pods and controlled ReplicaSet rollouts
definition: A workload controller that manages ReplicaSets to roll out and maintain replaceable stateless-style Pods.

name: StatefulSet
keywords: stable ordinal and storage identity
definition: A workload controller providing stable Pod identity, ordered lifecycle, and per-Pod claim templates.

name: Job
keywords: run Pods to successful completion
definition: A workload controller whose desired state is a specified number of successful Pod completions.

name: PodDisruptionBudget
keywords: limit voluntary evictions
definition: A policy that constrains API-initiated voluntary disruption according to minimum availability or maximum unavailability.

name: HPA versus VPA
keywords: replica count versus resource requests
definition: The distinction between horizontally changing replicas and vertically recommending or changing Pod resource requests.

name: CustomResourceDefinition
keywords: register a new API resource and schema
definition: A cluster-scoped object registering group, versions, kind, names, scope, and schema for a custom resource.

name: spec/status separation
keywords: intent versus observation
definition: The API convention that desired user intent belongs in spec while controller observations belong in status.

name: structural schema
keywords: CRD OpenAPI shape for pruning defaulting and apply
definition: A CRD schema shape required for reliable validation, pruning, defaulting, and server-side apply behavior.

name: served versus storage version
keywords: API representation versus persisted representation
definition: Served versions are requestable representations; exactly one storage version is used for newly persisted writes.

name: owner references versus finalizers
keywords: garbage collection relationship versus deletion cleanup gate
definition: Owner references express dependency for garbage collection; finalizers delay physical deletion until owned cleanup completes.

name: Scheduling Framework
keywords: filter score reserve permit bind plugins
definition: The pluggable kube-scheduler architecture organizing each placement attempt into scheduling and binding extension points.

name: resource requests
keywords: scheduler capacity currency
definition: Declared CPU, memory, and other resource quantities used by the scheduler for feasibility rather than live utilization.

name: placement constraints
keywords: hard filters and soft preferences
definition: Required and preferred rules including affinity, taints, topology, ports, and volumes that constrain or rank nodes.

name: Pod priority and preemption
keywords: displace lower-priority victims for pending Pod
definition: Scheduler behavior that orders Pods and may nominate removal of lower-priority Pods to make placement feasible.

name: preemption versus eviction
keywords: scheduler placement versus node pressure or voluntary disruption
definition: Preemption is a scheduler placement mechanism; eviction terminates Pods through node pressure or the Eviction API.

name: Container Runtime Interface
keywords: kubelet to runtime gRPC contract
definition: The gRPC contract through which kubelet manages Pod sandboxes, containers, images, and runtime status.

name: Pod sandbox
keywords: Pod isolation and network namespace anchor
definition: The runtime-created isolation context that anchors Pod-level namespaces and network attachment before normal containers run.

name: startup, liveness, and readiness probes
keywords: startup gating restart health and endpoint eligibility
definition: Distinct kubelet checks controlling startup protection, container restart, and traffic eligibility.

name: Pod QoS and cgroups
keywords: resource enforcement and eviction signals
definition: Resource classifications and kernel control groups that shape CPU, memory, OOM, and node-pressure behavior.

name: Pod termination lifecycle
keywords: grace period hooks TERM endpoint removal force
definition: The asynchronous process coordinating deletion grace, lifecycle hooks, signals, endpoint readiness, and eventual forceful stop.

name: Container Network Interface
keywords: configure Pod network attachment
definition: The runtime interface used by network plugins to attach Pod sandboxes to networks and allocate connectivity.

name: Service and EndpointSlice
keywords: stable virtual identity and ready backends
definition: A Service defines stable exposure semantics while EndpointSlices represent its current addresses, ports, readiness, and topology.

name: kube-proxy backends
keywords: node Service forwarding implementations
definition: Alternative implementations that program node-local Service virtual-IP forwarding while preserving Service semantics.

name: eBPF Service data plane
keywords: replace kube-proxy at kernel hooks
definition: A Service implementation using eBPF programs and maps at kernel hooks instead of traditional kube-proxy netfilter paths.

name: connection tracking
keywords: stateful flow and reverse translation memory
definition: State that associates packets with flows so return traffic, translation, and load-balancing decisions remain consistent.

name: cluster DNS resolution path
keywords: resolver to DNS Service to CoreDNS
definition: The path from an application resolver and Pod configuration through cluster DNS to a synthesized or upstream answer.

name: CoreDNS plugin chain
keywords: ordered DNS middleware
definition: The ordered plugins in a CoreDNS server block that answer, modify, observe, cache, fall through, or forward queries.

name: DNS search paths and ndots
keywords: query expansion and external lookup amplification
definition: Resolver rules controlling whether a name is tried with search suffixes before or after absolute lookup.

name: NodeLocal DNSCache
keywords: per-node DNS cache and shorter query path
definition: A per-node caching DNS agent that can reduce cluster DNS load and UDP connection-tracking pressure while adding another cache layer.
source: course/upstream; supplied video did not substantiate

name: headless Service DNS
keywords: return endpoint addresses without a ClusterIP
definition: DNS behavior for a Service with no virtual IP, returning backing endpoint addresses for client-side discovery.

name: PV, PVC, and StorageClass
keywords: capacity request and dynamic provisioning policy
definition: The storage API split between cluster capacity, a namespaced claim, and provisioning/binding parameters.

name: CSI controller sidecars
keywords: provision attach resize snapshot controllers
definition: External controllers that watch Kubernetes storage objects and call CSI controller RPCs for lifecycle operations.

name: CSI node stage and publish
keywords: prepare device and expose mount to Pod
definition: Node-side CSI operations that prepare a volume on a node and publish it at the workload-specific target path.

name: WaitForFirstConsumer
keywords: delay provisioning until placement topology known
definition: A volume binding mode delaying provisioning or binding until a consuming Pod's scheduling constraints identify compatible topology.

name: volume attachment lifecycle
keywords: attach mount reclaim and finalization
definition: The control- and node-plane process connecting provisioned capacity to a node, mounting it, and later detaching or reclaiming it safely.

name: Raft quorum
keywords: floor N over 2 plus 1
definition: The majority of consensus members required to commit writes while preserving a single agreed log.

name: etcd WAL and snapshot
keywords: durable log and compacted state backup
definition: The write-ahead log durably records consensus entries while snapshots compact and back up the resulting key-value state.

name: control-plane high availability
keywords: replaceable API servers and quorum-backed storage
definition: An architecture using redundant API servers and control-plane processes around an available etcd consensus group and stable endpoint.

name: leader election and Leases
keywords: one active writer and lightweight liveness
definition: Lease-based coordination used for active controller/scheduler leadership and efficient node heartbeat signaling.

name: control-plane disaster recovery
keywords: verified snapshot plus PKI configuration and workload recovery
definition: The rehearsed restoration of API state and surrounding control-plane dependencies to meet defined recovery objectives.

name: API Priority and Fairness
keywords: protect API server concurrency from overload
definition: API-server flow control that classifies requests, queues or rejects excess work, and allocates bounded concurrency among priority levels.

name: FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration
keywords: classify request flow and assign concurrency policy
definition: The APF objects that match request flows and assign their queueing, rejection, and concurrency behavior.

name: APF seats and queues
keywords: estimated concurrency cost and fair waiting
definition: The accounting and queueing mechanisms used to bound concurrent API work and share capacity across flows.

name: watch and informer scalability
keywords: shared caches relists and fan-out pressure
definition: The system impact of list-watch clients, cache sharing, object size, reconnection, and notification fan-out on API and etcd load.

name: Events, logs, metrics, and audit evidence
keywords: current state versus transition component aggregate and request evidence
definition: Complementary evidence types with different producers, retention, granularity, and authority for diagnosing Kubernetes behavior.
